column4: MAKI02 16-colour patch at (194,125)-(262,146). The encoder drops the last flag-A bit, so the last colour read runs 2 bytes past EOF and RECOIL rejects it. With 2 zero bytes appended, RECOIL's output is identical to ours. Forcing that bit consumes flag B and the colour stream exactly and gives the same pixels, so the result is unambiguous. Render shows a coherent eye-and-glasses crop.

MAKI02 2x1 patch at (622,332) from the same encoder (last flag-A bit dropped, colour read 2 bytes past EOF), so RECOIL rejects it. With 2 bytes appended, RECOIL matches ours. Either reading of the flag gives 8 pixels of palette colour 0.

Screen 8 BSAVE 0000-60B4, consistent with the file length. RECOIL rejects every Screen 7/8/12 dump shorter than 212 lines, but floors partial lines for Screen 5/6 (black-box probe). We apply that same rule: 96 complete lines, dropping 181 bytes of 0xFF on line 97. Render shows a title and sprite sheet with intact box borders.
Screen 8 BSAVE 0000-C000 (192 lines + 1 byte), consistent with the file length. RECOIL rejects Screen 8 dumps under 212 lines (black-box probe). Render shows a clean 4x3 grid of face frames.

Screen 8 dump whose 7 BSAVE header bytes are zero; the body is exactly 0xD400 bytes (212 lines). RECOIL needs the FE header. With the header restored to FE 0000 FFD3 0000, RECOIL's output is identical to ours. Render shows anime art signed C.H.PICOLO.
Screen 12 BSAVE dump (FE 0000 FFD3) saved with the extension .S12, which RECOIL does not list. Renamed to .SCC, RECOIL's output is identical to ours. Render shows a photo of the S1985 chip.
Screen 12 BSAVE dump (FE 0000 FFD3) with the extension .S12. Renamed to .SCC, RECOIL's output is identical to ours. Render shows a photo of a face (eyes).

Big-endian MAKI02 variant from an X68000 game: no machine name, every header field big-endian. RECOIL reads the header little-endian and rejects it. Flag A, flag B and colour streams are consumed exactly as sized (1 trailing pad byte). Render shows a coherent snowy-night scene.
